text:
182. Example 2: Explanation to the jury where a defendant has an intermediary
“During this trial, D will be helped by [name], who is an intermediary.
Intermediaries are used when a defendant needs help to understand what is being said in
court. If a defendant gives evidence, intermediaries are also used to make sure that
everyone in court understands what D is saying. The intermediary will intervene if they feel D
is having difficulty understanding something or needs a break.

117 [2011] EWCA Crim 3028.

118 Wording of examples taken from the Judicial College’s Crown Court Compendium (2025), chapter 3-7.
Children, young people and vulnerable adults
Equal Treatment Bench Book – July 2024 (February 2026 update) 63
The intermediary does not discuss the evidence with the defendant or give evidence for the
defendant.
Before today, the intermediary met and got to know D, and now the intermediary will help
D to follow the proceedings.
At an earlier hearing it was decided how D would be asked questions, for how long and in
what way. The intermediary helped the court make these decisions.
The fact that D is being helped by an intermediary must not affect how you assess any of
the evidence in this case and it is no reflection on D [if appropriate: or any other D].”
